title: Ulam–Kelly reconstruction conjecture for graph homomorphism counts
statement: Let $Hom(F,G)$ denote the number of graph homomorphisms from $F$ to $G$, and let $\mathcal{G}$ be the family of all graphs. For a family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, say that $Hom(\mathcal{F},\cdot)$ is reconstructible if, for every graph $G$ with at least three vertices, the vector of homomorphism counts $Hom(\mathcal{F},G)$ is uniquely determined by the vectors $Hom(\mathcal{F},G\setminus i)$ for every vertex $i$ of $G$. **Ulam–Kelly reconstruction conjecture.** $Hom(\mathcal{G},\cdot)$ is reconstructible. This is the homomorphism-count formulation of the Ulam–Kelly graph reconstruction conjecture, asserting that a graph with at least three vertices is determined up to isomorphism by the collection of its vertex-deleted subgraphs. The source presents this formulation as a motivation and question; no resolution is given here.
source_name: Thomás Jung Spier, “Efficient reconstruction of the characteristic polynomial”, arXiv:2503.17853 (2025).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2502.12781](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12781).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17853

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).
